summary: USNA exhibits the canonical MLM late-cycle distress signature with the strongest tells coming from Mode-B internal-consistency derivations rather than overt headline claims. SEVERE signals: (1) active Customer count down 6% to 454k vs the company's OWN PSU performance target of 584k by FYE2025 — management's compensation footnote already concedes 'not probable' and granted no new PSUs in 2024, the cleanest forward signal in the filing; (2) every disclosed market is in local-currency decline including China -1.7%, South Korea -19.5%, Philippines -18.6%, US -7.8% — a 2-year, 14.4% revenue erosion that is broad, not cyclical; (3) the December 2024 Hiya acquisition closed 5 days before FYE for $206M cash at 2.4x revenue and is admittedly GAAP-dilutive (pro forma NI would have been $31M vs reported $42M = -25%), with a 2028 put right requiring future US-cash payment; (4) US-domestic cash collapsed 76% to $40M while $101M of remaining cash sits SAFE-restricted in China, and the revolver was drawn from $0.8M to $23M — the balance sheet was structurally transformed in one quarter from net-cash MLM to cash-constrained integrating holdco. RED FLAG: 48.4% revenue concentration in a Chinese subsidiary operating on a model the Chinese government has explicitly NOT approved and where direct-selling-license expansion has been frozen since 2019. MODERATE: 2023 ITGC material weakness only freshly remediated; KPMG CAM on Hiya intangibles flags fair-value subjectivity on a 5-day-old deal; buyback shut off in Q4 2024 (zero repurchases) coincident with Hiya negotiation. Mitigants: CFO stable (8-yr tenure), no going-concern language, unqualified KPMG opinion, gross margin up 30bps. Net: strong SHORT signal under the honesty-alpha framework — disclosures are technically compliant but the narrative pillars (Associate-first growth, Hiya-driven future, healthy liquidity) are quantifiably inconsistent with management's own forward metrics.
